messages:
maya: Quick async q — who's allowed to flip the emergency_override feature for realtime-inference? We're doing a tabletop and need to confirm auth, audit flow, and canary scope.
jonathan: Ops rotation + Eng SRE leads can flip. We also have a secondary whitelist for Platform leads.
paula: To add: flipping is gated by MFA + 'reason' in the CLI so audit logs capture intent. But not everyone knows the exact command.
samir: Command is `flagctl set emergency_override off --reason "hotstop: noisy gpus" --tag incident-123` (internal flag service). It writes an audit entry to /audit/feature-flips.
maya: Nice — where does the audit entry surface? Console? SIEM?
jonathan: It posts to the console activity feed and to Splunk under index=redwood_audit with field `actor`, `reason`, `tag`, `before`, `after`. ops-rotation-bot also emits an ephemeral slack msg to #eng-oncall.
paula: Two policy items: 1) flips must be accompanied by a pager notification to the current oncall, and 2) a TTL of 30m should be applied for non-critical flips unless explicitly extended.
samir: We have `--ttl` in flagctl. Example: `flagctl set emergency_override off --reason "safety-cut" --ttl 30m --tag incident-123`
maya: Who is the approver for >30m extensions?
jonathan: Platform oncall + the SRE lead on duty. If both aren't reachable, escalate to Eng Manager oncall. Document the approval in the incident ticket.
paula: Also: for canary audiences — the toggle supports audience scoping. Don't flip globally unless traffic is already blocked. For canary, use `audience=canary:realtime-10pct`.
samir: Right. And add metrics watchlist: p99 latency, error-rate (500s), token throughput. We also have a guarded fallback that auto-rolls back if error-rate > 5% for 2 consecutive 1m windows.
maya: Where's the guardrail config stored? I want to link it in the tabletop doc.
jonathan: In repo infra/ops/guardrails.yaml and mirrored to the console. The file documents rollback thresholds per flag.
maya: Ok, one last: audit chain of custody — if someone from Platform flips and then hands back to Ops during incident, how do we record that handoff?
paula: We require a comment on the ticket and the flag flip `--tag` should reference the ticket ID plus `handed-to:<name>`. Example: `--tag incident-123 handed-to:ops-team` so it shows up in audit queries.
samir: We also have a tiny helper: `flagctl handoff --flag emergency_override --to ops-oncall --ticket incident-123` which creates the audit annotation and posts a slack thread.
maya: Perfect. I'll add these to the tabletop checklist. Can someone paste the minimal runbook snippet for the oncall?
jonathan: Snippet:```
1) Notify oncall channel: /msg @ops-oncall "issuing emergency_override off for realtime-inference — reason + ticket"
2) Run: flagctl set emergency_override off --reason "<reason>" --ttl 30m --tag incident-<id>
3) Watch: p99 latency, 500s errors, token throughput for 10m
4) If errors spike, run: flagctl rollback emergency_override --tag incident-<id>
5) Record handoff: flagctl handoff --flag emergency_override --to <team> --ticket <id>```
paula: I'll PR the checklist into docs/playbooks and add links to the guardrail yaml and the Splunk query.
ops-rotation-bot: Reminder: current ops rotation is @samir until 2024-08-12. For emergencies ping @samir directly. :bell:
deploy-bot: Audit entry created when commands run. Make sure `--reason` is non-empty or the CLI will reject the flip.
maya: Thanks all — saving notes and will sync with PM for the tabletop timeline. :thumbsup:
